title: Delete and delegation-child removal drop a retained non-Confirmed cleanup lease
outcome: Delete and delegation-child removal drop a retained non-Confirmed cleanup lease
acceptance: On Windows, Delete of a local session or its delegated-child subtree refuses removal while any affected dedicated runtime cleanup owner is InProgress or Unconfirmed, including retained predecessors. The affected session/card and exact retry ownership remain visible through the existing session state and cards (this item makes no UI change); refusal must not partially remove the subtree or report confirmed cleanup.

Cancelling or settling a delegated child does not discard an exact dedicated-runtime cleanup owner on failed or unknown teardown. The visible child reports the cleanup failure and has a working public Stop retry; successful cleanup is confirmed by job-zero/native process exit before ownership is released.

Healthy Delete remains usable and removes its intended subtree after successful scoped cleanup. Cleanup waits run outside StateInner, and stale cleanup completion cannot remove a replacement runtime/session or a concurrently changed affected subtree. Windows native-process regressions distinguish failed cleanup, successful retry, healthy deletion, retained predecessor and final revalidation; the exact final input passes the maintained full gate and the independent Codex/Claude read-only pair has no unresolved in-scope Medium or higher.
